clue.text: Something the barber may rub around?

definitions.text: Something the barber may rub around?

parts.words: Something the barber may rub around?
parts.note: a scented hair lotion that a barber massages into a customer's scalp, the question mark hinting at a rubbing motion

explanation.surface: A puzzle about what a barber might massage into the hair.
explanation.walkthrough: Bay rum is a traditional fragrant tonic made from bay leaves and rum, splashed on by barbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Bay rum is a scented hair and skin lotion traditionally applied in barbershops.

clue.text: Chief means of support

definitions.meaning: a curved structure holding up a bridge or roof

explanation.definitionFit: Arch as an adjective means principal, and as a noun a curved load-bearing structure.

clue.text: Hooligan displays sheer audacity on part of the golf course

indicators.note: the cheek is placed on, or attached after, the golf-course area, so it comes second

parts.note: the rough is the long grass beside the fairway
neck is British slang for cheek or nerve

explanation.surface: A thug shows brazen cheek out on the links.
explanation.definitionFit: A roughneck is a rowdy, uncouth person, a synonym for a thug.

clue.text: Phone for port in Alabama

definitions.meaning: the Gulf Coast city on ... Bay

explanation.definitionFit: A mobile is a cell phone, and Mobile is Alabama's chief seaport.

clue.text: New form of travel in space

indicators.note: giving the words a new form means rearranging their letters into another word

explanation.surface: A novel way of journeying through outer space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New form of' rearranges TRAVEL and IN; 'space' looks like outer space but means a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: An interval is a gap or space between two things, in time or distance.

clue.text: The resolution of endless ambition?

indicators.note: resolving the words breaks them down and works them out again into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: What firm resolve looks like when ambition never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: unending ambition shows unshakable resolution.
explanation.definitionFit: Indomitableness is the quality of refusing to be subdued, a dogged resolve.

clue.text: Matchbox model

parts.note: not a toy car but a legal precedent that shows how such disputes will be decided, the 'match' being a contest

explanation.surface: A die-cast toy car from a well-known range.
explanation.walkthrough: Matchbox is a British brand of toy cars; read instead as a box for a match (a contest), a model suit in court.
explanation.definitionFit: A test case is a legal action whose outcome sets the pattern for others.

clue.text: Disturb with sound arguments

indicators.note: sound signals that the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: rows, rhyming with cows, are quarrels

explanation.surface: Wake someone with convincing points.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse is to wake or stir someone, disturbing their rest.

clue.text: Be thankful for rise in value

definitions.meaning: to value or be grateful for
grow in worth, as property does

explanation.definitionFit: To appreciate is both to be grateful for something and to increase in worth.

clue.text: Took out and cleaned

definitions.meaning: cancelled or deleted, as a planned event is struck off

explanation.definitionFit: To scrub a plan is to cancel it, and to scrub a floor is to clean it vigorously.

clue.text: Cricket fixtures finally drawn

parts.note: the wooden uprights fixed in the ground at a cricket pitch, which are pulled up at the close of play

explanation.surface: Cricket matches that ended in a draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fixtures' suggests scheduled matches and 'drawn' a tied result; in cricket, 'drawing stumps' means pulling them up to end the day's play.
explanation.definitionFit: The stumps are the three upright posts fixed into the ground at each end of a cricket pitch.

clue.text: An angelfish? Gracious!

definitions.meaning: whimsically, a fish that is saintly or sacred
an exclamation of surprise, like 'Good heavens!'

explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation of astonishment literally names a sacred mackerel, playfully a heavenly fish.

clue.text: Train officer, one of the same class

parts.note: to school someone is to teach or train them
a mate is an officer on a merchant ship

explanation.surface: A railway official sharing a carriage class with passengers.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmate is a fellow pupil, someone in the same school class.

clue.text: A conservative leader about to give ground

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: re is Latin-derived shorthand meaning concerning or about

explanation.surface: A Tory chief is about to concede territory.
explanation.definitionFit: An acre is a unit of land area, so ground measured out in plots.

clue.text: It's a man in distress on a South Pacific island

indicators.note: something in distress is wrecked or disordered, signalling these letters are scrambled

parts.note: read as it is, giving its three letters

explanation.surface: Someone is in trouble on a remote island in southern waters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Distress' suggests a castaway in trouble, but it scrambles the letters; 'on' attaches the final A.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasmania is the island state off south-east Australia, bordering the southern Pacific.

clue.text: A great thinker tries a lot to be different

indicators.note: making the letters different means rearranging them

explanation.surface: A philosopher works hard to stand out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be different' rearranges TRIES, A and LOT.
explanation.definitionFit: Aristotle was the ancient Greek philosopher, one of history's foremost minds.

clue.text: Mistakes made by bakers, underwear suppliers and gardeners?

definitions.text: Mistakes made by bakers, underwear suppliers and gardeners?

parts.words: Mistakes made by bakers, underwear suppliers and gardeners?
parts.note: one word for slips that also names a crusty loaf, baggy knickers and flowering plants

explanation.surface: Errors committed by three different trades.
explanation.walkthrough: The word means blunders, a loaf with a slashed top, old-fashioned knickers and plants in flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Bloomers are blunders, and also loaves, voluminous knickers and blossoming plants.

clue.text: Agency that sends work to you at home

definitions.text: Agency that sends work to you at home

parts.words: Agency that sends work to you at home
parts.note: not an employment agency but a subscription service that posts literary works to members' homes

explanation.surface: A firm that arranges home-working jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' suggests employment; it is a literary work, a book, mailed to subscribers.
explanation.definitionFit: A book club is a mail-order subscription scheme that sends books to members.

clue.text: I take round thank-you letter

parts.note: the circular letter O looks round
ta is British informal speech for thanks

explanation.surface: Someone takes a note of thanks around personally.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Winner takes part in rousing game

definitions.meaning: a role at a shoot, flushing out birds for the guns

explanation.definitionFit: A beater defeats rivals, and at a shoot drives game birds into the open.

clue.text: Unsuitable piece of music for a quickstep?

definitions.text: Unsuitable piece of music for a quickstep?

parts.words: Unsuitable piece of music for a quickstep?
parts.note: a fast ballroom dance would be badly served by an unhurried section of a symphony

explanation.surface: A dance band chooses the wrong tune for a fast dance.
explanation.walkthrough: A quickstep is a brisk ballroom dance; a symphony's leisurely section, such as an adagio, would not suit it.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow movement is the unhurried section of a larger musical work like a symphony.

clue.text: Joyful shout of TV doctor given work

parts.note: the Time Lord of the long-running BBC science-fiction series
op is short for opus, a musical work

explanation.surface: A cheer from a television physician once employed.
explanation.walkthrough: Doctor Who is the BBC science-fiction hero; OP (opus) is a work.
explanation.definitionFit: A whoop is a loud cry of excitement or delight.

clue.text: Country putting physical education over sport

indicators.note: in a down answer, one piece placed over another comes first

parts.note: PE is the school abbreviation
RU stands for rugby union

explanation.surface: A nation puts gym classes ahead of games.
explanation.definitionFit: Peru is a South American nation on the Pacific coast.

clue.text: Deadly to John, she's also awful to me

indicators.note: something awful is a mess, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A woman fatal to a man called John is also dreadful to the speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: Herod's stepdaughter demanded the head of John the Baptist as her reward for dancing; 'awful' makes SALO.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Gospels, Salome's dance led Herod to have John the Baptist beheaded.

clue.text: Championship secured in final with style

indicators.note: something held inside another is enclosed by it

parts.note: the final part is the end
a title is a championship won in a sport

explanation.surface: A trophy was won stylishly in the closing match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with style' means given a title or style, as a lord is entitled.
explanation.definitionFit: Being entitled means bearing a formal title or style of address.

clue.text: They may be allowed to share secrets, being upright

definitions.text: They may be allowed to share secrets, being upright

parts.words: They may be allowed to share secrets, being upright
parts.note: alludes to the saying 'between you, me and the' piece of bedroom furniture, said when confiding a secret

explanation.surface: Honest people may be trusted with confidences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upright' suggests honesty but means standing vertical, like the corner posts of a bed.
explanation.definitionFit: Bedposts are the upright corner posts of a bedstead, invoked in a confiding phrase.

clue.text: Primate replaces ushers

indicators.note: the letters are placed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A senior churchman takes over from the cinema attendants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' looks like an archbishop in this surface; it is the monkey.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhesus is a macaque monkey, a member of the primate order.
